title: Sandpiper Point Rising Revisited
premise: Coral Quintana has spent a decade guarding her heart and her grandfather's lighthouse on Sandpiper Point, writing romance novels under a pseudonym while keeping her real love life in the past tense. When the town's winter literary festival assigns anonymous pen-pals to boost morale after a devastating storm, Coral is paired with Eli Marsh—the coastal commissioner whose development plans threaten to condemn her lighthouse as unsafe. Through letters that never reveal names, they fall for each other's truest selves, until Coral discovers her correspondent is the very man trying to erase her family's legacy. In the end, Eli must choose between his career and testifying against his own firm at the heritage hearing, and Coral must decide whether a man who loved her honestly in ink can be trusted with her whole heart in person.
about_author: Ada Okonkwo is a former maritime archivist who spent five years cataloguing lighthouse keeper logs along the Atlantic seaboard before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted boathouse, where she insists every love story deserves both a storm and a safe harbor.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the storm-battered Sandpiper Point literary festival, Coral reluctantly joins the anonymous pen-pal program meant to lift the town's spirits, receiving a first letter that is sharp, funny, and unexpectedly honest. She replies without knowing she's writing to Eli Marsh, the man who publicly called her lighthouse 'a liability.' Emotional beat: guarded curiosity—a door left unlatched.

chapters.title: Letters in the Dark
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Coral and Eli. Over weeks of correspondence, both confess things they've told no one—her stalled novel and grief for her grandfather; his suffocating loyalty to the firm that raised him. Meanwhile, in daylight, their public clashes over the lighthouse condemnation grow uglier. Emotional beat: intimacy deepening in secret while hostility hardens in public, dramatic irony tightening like a knot.

chapters.title: The Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: Eli's POV, then Coral's. Eli recognizes Coral's handwriting on a festival submission and realizes who his pen-pal is just as his firm moves up the demolition hearing. He signs his next letter with his real name; Coral reads it hours after he votes to condemn the lighthouse. Emotional beat: betrayal and reckoning—she burns the letters, then can't make herself burn the last one.

chapters.title: What the Lighthouse Keeps
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the heritage hearing, Eli testifies against his own firm, exposing falsified inspection reports and saving the lighthouse—then waits outside in the rain, unclaimed. Coral must choose between the wound and the man who wrote her the truth twice: once anonymously, once at cost. Emotional beat: resolution—she lends him no pieces this time, only the whole heart, as the light comes on above them.
